descs.t: Donald Trump's rally in Chillicothe, Ohio was interrupted by protesters shouting that he went on Jeffrey Epstein's plane, with at least three hauled out in the first few minutes. Trump answered that he threw Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. We walk through the footage, the hecklers and how Trump responded.

Minutes into Trump's Ohio rally, protesters started yelling about Jeffrey Epstein's plane, one after another, until security removed them. Trump's supporters call them paid protesters; one heckler posted his own footage of being pulled out. We look at what happened, what Trump said back about Epstein, and why the attack line keeps coming.

Heckler after heckler tried to derail Donald Trump's rally in Chillicothe, Ohio with Epstein taunts, and Trump fired back that he threw Jeffrey Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. Here is the raw footage, the protesters who planned it, and how the crowd and the president handled it.

intro.plain: Trump's rally in Chillicothe, Ohio did not go to plan. Minutes in, protesters started shouting that Trump went on Jeffrey Epstein's plane, and at least three were hauled out. Trump answered that he threw Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. Chat, what do you make of it: real protest or a stunt?
intro.mid: Five minutes. That is how long Trump's Ohio rally ran before the Epstein hecklers started, one after another, until security pulled them out. Trump's answer: he threw Jeffrey Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. His fans say these were paid protesters. Chat, my question: does this kind of heckling help or hurt the people doing it?
intro.bold: They came to Trump's rally in Ohio with one line, Epstein's plane, and they used it one after another. Security pulled them out, and Trump hit back that he threw Epstein out of his club about 20 years ago. The crowd did not budge. Chat, be honest: did the hecklers win this one, or did Trump?

descs.t: Vivek Ramaswamy, the Republican candidate for Ohio governor, joined Donald Trump on stage at a rally in Chillicothe, Ohio, promising the biggest property tax relief in the state and action by executive order on his first day. Senator Jon Husted also spoke. We walk through what Ramaswamy promised and how the night went.

Donald Trump flew to Chillicothe, Ohio to campaign for Vivek Ramaswamy, who pitched lower property taxes and electric bills, safer streets and better schools, plus a day one executive order. We look at his promises, the crowd's reaction, and whether the rally can move votes in the governor's race.

Vivek Ramaswamy took the stage with Donald Trump in Chillicothe, Ohio and the crowd erupted, with chants of USA through the night. He promised Ohio its biggest property tax relief and action on day one by executive order. Here is the rally, the promises and why Republicans think Ohio is theirs.

Chat, my question: is a rally like this enough to win a governor's race?

descs.t: President Trump is calling for Democratic Alaska Senate candidate Mary Peltola to be prosecuted after reports that her campaign looked for a second Dan Sullivan to put on the ballot against Senator Dan Sullivan. Alaska Governor Mike Dunleavy has ordered an investigation, and reports say the DOJ has opened a criminal probe. We walk through what was reported, who is involved and what could happen next.

The Alaska decoy candidate story has gone from a New York Times report to a criminal investigation in a day, with Trump and JD Vance calling for consequences and Peltola dismissing it as a distraction. Republicans say a same name candidate was meant to confuse voters; her defenders say it is not illegal. We look at the evidence, the legal questions and what it means for the Senate race.

A fake Dan Sullivan on Alaska's Senate ballot, reportedly recruited to confuse voters, has put Mary Peltola's campaign under investigation and Trump is demanding prosecution. JD Vance says she is trying to steal a Senate seat. We break down what the reports say her team did, why it matters for every voter and whether anyone will be charged.

intro.plain: Big story out of Alaska. President Trump is calling for Democratic Senate candidate Mary Peltola to be prosecuted after reports her campaign searched for a second Dan Sullivan to run against Senator Dan Sullivan. Alaska's governor has ordered an investigation, and reports say the DOJ is looking at it too. So let me ask you in the chat: should a same name candidate like this be a crime?
intro.mid: Here is the story everyone is fighting about today. Reports say Mary Peltola's people went looking for another Dan Sullivan to put on Alaska's ballot. Peltola calls it a distraction. Trump wants her prosecuted, JD Vance wants an investigation, and Alaska's governor has already ordered one. Tell me in the chat: is this dirty politics as usual, or is it fraud?
intro.bold: They found a second Dan Sullivan and put him on the ballot. That is what reports say happened in Alaska's Senate race, and now Mary Peltola's campaign is under investigation. Trump wants her prosecuted. JD Vance says she is trying to steal a Senate seat. This is about whether voters get tricked at the ballot box. Chat, tell me: should she drop out of the race?

hook.bold: A fake Dan Sullivan, reportedly recruited to confuse voters, ended up on Alaska's ballot. Now Trump wants Peltola prosecuted. Here is how the scheme was exposed.

descs.t: Flávio Bolsonaro, the defeated candidate in Brazil's presidential runoff, has landed in Miami with his family after the US granted him entry, and says he is Brazil's rightful leader. The Washington Post reports he defied a Brazilian judicial order to surrender his passport. We walk through how he left, what his statement claims, and what Brazil's courts can do now.

Flávio Bolsonaro lost Brazil's runoff to Lula, left the country against a court order, and now says from the United States that the election was stolen and he is the true president elect. Critics say he is fleeing a criminal investigation; supporters say federal police moved on his passport seven minutes after the result. We look at both claims and what Trump's decision to let him in means.

With his father Jair Bolsonaro behind bars, Flávio Bolsonaro got out of Brazil on a private jet and landed in Miami, where he declared himself Brazil's rightful leader and vowed to lead the opposition from the US. Lula's side calls him a fugitive. Here is how he escaped, why his allies call it political persecution, and what comes next for Brazil's right.

intro.plain: Brazil now has a defeated presidential candidate claiming the presidency from Florida. Flávio Bolsonaro landed in Miami with his family after the US let him in, and the Washington Post says he defied a court order to hand over his passport. Now he says he is Brazil's rightful leader. Chat, quick question: should the US have let him in?
intro.mid: Seven minutes. That is how fast, according to Michael Shellenberger, federal police moved on Flávio Bolsonaro's passport after Brazil's result came in. Now Bolsonaro is in Miami, calling the election stolen and calling himself president. His critics call him a fugitive from a criminal investigation. Chat, which is it: persecution or escape from justice?
intro.bold: Flávio Bolsonaro is out. His father is in prison, Brazil's courts wanted his passport, and he still made it to Miami on a private jet. Now he says Brazil's election was stolen and he will lead the opposition from abroad. Lula's people call him a fugitive. Chat, tell me straight: is this persecution of Brazil's right, or a man running from the law?

hook.plain: Brazil's defeated presidential candidate is now in Miami, saying he is the country's rightful leader. Here is how he left Brazil against a court order, and what happens now.
hook.mid: Police reportedly moved on his passport seven minutes after the result. Days later, Flávio Bolsonaro was in Miami calling himself president. Here is the full chain of events.
hook.bold: His father got 27 years. Brazil's courts wanted his passport. Flávio Bolsonaro got out anyway, and now he says he is Brazil's real president. Here is how he did it.
